title: Efficient removal of Pb(II) and Zn(II) ions from aqueous solutions by adsorption onto a native natural bentonite
author: Esmaeili, Eslami

steps.title: Crush and sieve bentonite
steps.instruction: Crush the native natural bentonite (NNB) using a jaw crusher (Pulverisette, Fritsch, Germany) and sieve the material, retaining particles that pass a 50‑mesh screen.

steps.title: Dry the sieved material
steps.instruction: Dry the sieved NNB at laboratory temperature with ambient air flow for two weeks.

steps.title: Determine chemical composition
steps.instruction: Analyze the dried NNB by X‑ray fluorescence (XRF) using a PHILIPS PW1730 (Netherlands) and record the following weight percentages: SiO₂ 64.0 wt %, Al₂O₃ 36.5 wt %, Fe₂O₃ 3.6 wt %, CaO 2.2 wt %, MgO 3.0 wt %, Na₂O 2.2 wt %, K₂O 0.5 wt %, LOI 10.7 wt %.

steps.title: Measure cation exchange capacity
steps.instruction: Measure the CEC of the NNB by the Methylene Blue Index method according to ASTM C 837‑81 and note the mineralogical composition (Montmorillonite 94.6 %, Illite, Quartz) and the CEC value (meq / 100 g) as reported.

steps.title: Prepare metal ion solutions
steps.instruction: Using analytical‑grade reagents (≥99 % purity, Merck), prepare 50 mL aqueous solutions of Pb(II) or Zn(II) at an initial concentration of 50 mg L⁻¹ and adjust the pH to 3.0 ± 0.1.

steps.title: Set up batch adsorption
steps.instruction: In a 300 mL flat‑bottom Erlenmeyer flask, add a defined amount of NNB (0.2 g to 1.2 g), then add the 50 mL metal solution. Place the flask on a rotary shaker set to 150 rpm, maintain the temperature at 27 ± 1 °C, and agitate for 300 min.

steps.title: Determine residual metal concentration
steps.instruction: After agitation, separate the solid (e.g., by filtration) and measure the remaining Pb(II) or Zn(II) concentration in the supernatant using atomic absorption spectroscopy (Varian AA‑975 or AA‑1275, Perkin Elmer).

steps.title: Calculate adsorption capacity
steps.instruction: Compute the amount of metal adsorbed per gram of NNB (qₑ, mg g⁻¹) using the equation qₑ = (C₀ – Cₑ) × V / m, where C₀ is the initial concentration (mg L⁻¹), Cₑ the equilibrium concentration (mg L⁻¹), V the solution volume (L), and m the mass of adsorbent (g).
